line: Jung's passages naming the seven: the planetary gods, the seven metals, the archons and the colours of the work; Pauli's reading of the seven in his dream, and von Franz on seven.

sections.title: What Jung names
sections.line: CW12 ¶83 (in the language of initiation), CW14 ¶563 (the gods of the planets, or the seven metals) and a note to CW9i ¶242 (the seven as the planetary gods of the ancients). Jung writes no essay on seven; these are places where he names it.

quotes.quote: In the language of initiation, “seven” stands for the highest stage of illumination
The “seven” refer to the gods of the planets, or the seven metals
The seven are the planetary gods of the ancients.

sections.title: Gods, metals and archons
sections.line: CW12 ¶468 (the seven gods in the metals of alchemy), CW12 ¶298 (the seven Babylonian gods and the seven Archons, in the Book of Enoch), CW13 ¶409 (the seven metals and the seven planets, in the tree) and CW14 ¶576 (the seven archons of the Ophite diagram as the seven planets).

quotes.quote: The historical sousentendu of the seven is the antique company of seven gods who later took up their abode in the seven metals of alchemy
Originally the seven stars were the seven great Babylonian gods, but at the time of Enoch’s revelation they had become the seven Archons
Its connection with the seven metals implies a connection with the seven planets, so that the tree becomes the world-tree
The seven archons correspond to the seven planets and represent so many spheres with doors which the celebrant has to pass through on his ascent

sections.title: The stages of the work, and the week
sections.line: CW14 ¶390 (the seven colours of the work, associated with the planets) and ¶579 (the archetype of the seven in the division of the week).

quotes.quote: The stages of the work are marked by seven colours which are associated with the planets
The archetype of the seven appears again in the division of the week and the naming of its days

sections.title: Pauli and von Franz
sections.line: Pauli's letter 16P (1936) on the seven in his early dreams; von Franz on the Mayan seven-one gods, Bruno's forty-nine planetary images (seven per planet) and the numbers three and seven in the Lo-shu figure.

quotes.quote: So the 7 is an indication of the birth of the anima.
In the Mayan culture, for instance, so-called seven-one-gods play an outstanding role.
the forty-nine planetary images (seven per planet)
the numbers three and seven to his right and left
